# Melting

## Learning objectives
1. State the melting point of pure water at standard pressure.
2. Explain why the temperature stays constant while a pure solid melts.

## Melting point of pure water
At standard pressure the melting point of pure water is 0 °C.

The substance this chapter anchors on is water: {{smiles O}}

## What the source says
The synthetic handbook records the value directly: "the melting point of pure water at standard pressure is 0 °C" — a direct quotation, reproduced verbatim from a public-domain fixture source.

## Latent heat of fusion
Melting pure water absorbs 334 J/g of latent heat of fusion while the temperature stays constant.

## Synthesis
A pure solid melts at a characteristic temperature, and the energy supplied during melting goes into
the phase change rather than into a temperature rise.

:::: tabs
::: tab Worked example
How much energy melts 10 g of ice already at its melting point?
:::
::: tab Solution
Multiply the latent heat of fusion by the mass: 334 J/g times 10 g is 3340 J.
:::
::::
